title: Press Start - a playable video game history. Would love feedback.
author: SuruiMakesGames
selftext:
I've been building **Press Start** (pressstart.site) with Claude, a history of video games you play rather than read.

There are 27 stops from 1958 to 2025, covering the US and Japan. At each stop you play a short piece modelled on the game that defined that moment: tennis on a lab oscilloscope, a coin-op TV game in a bar, a cartridge console, a two-screen handheld where you draw with a stylus (it closes its lid when you leave), a time-rewind platformer, a phone puzzle game whose gacha machine prints its odds, a dock-to-handheld console with slide-on controllers, a VR saber game, and more. After each one, an exhibit card tells the real history, introduces the people behind it, and links to where you can play the originals today.

I'd really like feedback: which stops feel off, what history I got wrong, and what is missing. Thanks! And hope you enjoy the website.

replies.author: Anhedonia_Achiever
replies.body: Super cool! I love subscribing to this sub because I get to see posts like these that would’ve gotten insane love just a few years ago on Reddit. But every day it feels like someone’s pumping out something amazing. Hard to keep track.

comments.author: krazyjakee
comments.body: Was the 90s just a blip to you?

replies.author: SuruiMakesGames
replies.body: My knowdlege is limited haha. What stuff do you recommend me to add to the 90s?

replies.author: krazyjakee
replies.body: The console wars of the 90s mostly consisted of Genesis, SNES, N64 & PlayStation. Each were revolutionary in their own right. The jump to 3D and the gameplay and design that came with the earliest games were borderline miraculous with many of those fundamentals still implemented today in AAA titles.
